newsitem.title: CHINA: Tumen development group offers membership to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Tumen development group offers membership to Japan.

text.p: An international body working on a development plan for the Tumen river area in northeast Asia has offered Japan official membership in the group, China's Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

The Consultative Commission of the Tumen River Economic Development Area, now meeting in Beijing, had agreed on Tuesday to invite Japan to join, Xinhua quoted Long Yongtu, an official with China's Ministry of Foreign Trade, as saying.
China, Russia, North Korea, South Korea and Mongolia are the current members of the commission to develop the Tumen River delta, where the borders of China, Russia and North Korea meet.

The $30 billion, 20-year Tumen development scheme aims to slash export costs for huge landlocked swathes of northeast China, Siberia and Mongolia and lure Pacific Rim investment for resource exploitation, agriculture and industry.
Feasibility studies on the plan had been completed, and related work on transport and telecommunications networks was underway, Xinhua said.

The Tumen region had used a total of $526 million in foreign investment by mid-1996, with 50 percent of those funds going to Russia and 40 percent to China, Xinhua said. It gave no details of the remaining 10 percent.
